title: EFC Weak Lensing Phenomenology: A Testable μ(k,z) Framework and DES Y6 Validation Protocol
abstract_short: Testable μ(k,z) framework for weak lensing. Addresses S₈ tension (0.789 vs 0.83). Pass/fail criteria defined for DES Y6.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes the first dedicated weak-lensing phenomenology framework for EFC, deriving the scale- and redshift-dependent gravitational modification function μ(k,z) from Postulate A and constructing a complete DES Y6 validation protocol. It bridges the gap between EFC's core modified-gravity prediction and Stage-IV lensing data, providing the concrete machinery needed to test whether EFC's μ(k,z) structure can resolve the S₈ tension. This is a critical infrastructure paper that converts a theoretical distinctive signature into a falsifiable pipeline.
graph_insights: The graph shows no prior paper connected to weak lensing or μ(k,z) — this paper is a new leaf node that creates the first link between EFC's Postulate A cluster and the lensing-observable cluster, bridging a topological gap in the knowledge graph.

The connection to 'S₈ tension' creates a path from EFC core theory through μ(k,z) to the broader cosmological tensions literature, which was previously only connected through the fσ₈/growth channel — this doubles EFC's interface surface with observational cosmology.
No validation tests sharing observables were found in the graph, confirming this is genuinely new infrastructure rather than a refinement of existing tests.

ledger_impact.narrative_frame_reason: The paper does not close a kill criterion or falsify a competitor but clarifies and operationalises the weak-lensing channel, converting EFC's abstract μ(k,z) prediction into a concrete, testable DES Y6 protocol.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_sentence: EFC's scale-dependent μ(k,z) lensing signature is now operationalised with a full DES Y6 validation protocol, providing the first dedicated weak-lensing test infrastructure for the framework.
implicit_consequences: The μ(k,z) functional form, once confronted with DES Y6 data, will simultaneously constrain Postulate A's effective coupling — any tension in the lensing fit would propagate back as a constraint on the energy-dissipation rate, creating a cross-channel consistency requirement with the fσ₈ sealed prediction.

If DES Y6 shear data confirm EFC's μ(k,z), the S₈ tension resolution becomes an EFC-specific achievement that ΛCDM cannot replicate without additional free parameters, strengthening the framework's Bayesian evidence relative to ΛCDM+Σ extensions.

The protocol infrastructure defined here can be straightforwardly extended to Euclid and Rubin LSST shear catalogs, meaning this paper implicitly establishes the lensing validation pathway for the next decade of Stage-IV surveys.

The paper's μ(k,z) derivation from Postulate A creates a tight coupling between the weak-lensing channel and the ADM Hamiltonian stability gap (theory-adm-hamiltonian-stability): any instability found in the non-linear ADM sector could invalidate the μ(k,z) form at small scales, making the Hamiltonian stability gap more urgent.

The absence of a dedicated EFCLASS Boltzmann solver (theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver) means the DES Y6 protocol currently relies on modified CLASS or CAMB with injected μ(k,z) — full self-consistency requires closing that theory gap before the lensing tests can be considered definitive.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_change: Biggest gap remains DESI DR2 full-shape RSD rapid-response pipeline, but weak-lensing μ(k,z) DES Y6 protocol is now the second-priority pipeline deliverable. Test count should increase: total≈136, pipeline≈24.
